answer: A concrete rule the ledger can enforce: pay rewards over a slow vesting curve tied to continued correct work, because ocean only stays cheap while a farm must fund and babysit every clone for weeks before cashing anything out. In practice nadir is enforced by the ledger itself: Withdrawal limits start near zero and open only against a measured history of accepted answers. Any lantern approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
